title: Why do 10,000 birds never crash mid-air?

hook.narration: Ten thousand birds. One sky. Zero air traffic control.

scenes.narration: Starling murmurations twist like one creature — and they almost never hit each other.
Head-on collision course? Every bird plays the same two cards: veer right — and never at the same height.
fact_sources: Schiffner & Srinivasan 2016 (QBI Queensland): veer right + pass above/below

scenes.narration: No negotiation. No chatter. Just the rule. Every bird. Every time.
fact_sources: restate of the 2016 rule — no new claim

scenes.narration: The real cheat code: each starling tracks about seven neighbors. Not the flock. Seven.
fact_sources: Ballerini et al. 2008 PNAS: topological interaction, ~7 neighbors — 'about seven', never 'exactly'

scenes.narration: One bird turns — and the whole murmuration bends with it. One system. One move.
fact_sources: safe restatement: 'the whole murmuration bends with it' (approved phrasing)

scenes.narration: No towers. No radar. Seven friends and one rule.
Stuck in traffic? The birds solved it.

loop_line: Stuck in traffic? The birds solved it.
